Subject: Post-call: Deployment mode qualification + TCO scenarios

Hi John — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and agreed next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Summary of what we heard from Acme: 
- Primary priority: strict data residency and auditability for customer PII (legal requires EU/US controls), leaning toward Private VPC or on-prem for production.
- Secondary: 99th-percentile latency target of ~150ms for chat; expected steady-state generation volume ~18M tokens/day with occasional spikes to 50M tokens/day.
- Cost sensitivity: procurement needs a comparison of per-token hosted vs reserved dedicated commits with TCO across 12/24 month terms.

What Redwood will deliver (next 48–72h):
1) A TCO workbook with three scenarios (Hosted API, Dedicated Reserved, Private VPC) — assumptions spelled out per scenario. [Attachment: acme_tco_v1.xlsx]
2) Short one-page deployment-mode summary highlighting tradeoffs (latency, security, ops). [Attachment: redwood_deploy_modes_summary.pdf]
3) Schedule a pricing/procurement sync with your team (Lauren and I available Wed + Thu).

Immediate asks for Acme: 
- Confirm expected concurrency (avg and peak) and any hard SLOs beyond the chat 150ms 99p.
- Confirm whether the private option must be fully air-gapped or if a VPC with egress controls is acceptable.

Next internal owners: Vivek (SE) will lead the technical assumptions in the workbook; Monica (CS) will draft the migration/operational checklist; Lauren (sales lead) will coordinate the procurement conversation.

Thanks — Ben

--

Thanks Ben — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Concurrency / volume: the 18M tokens/day is our current forecast for feature rollout. Peak concurrency during business hours might reach ~120 concurrent sessions generating ~1.2k tokens each. Spikes could push concurrent sessions to ~400 for high-traffic events.
2) Data residency: For initial launch EU customers must have data stored within EU boundaries. A VPC deployment that keeps customer data within our EU cloud account is acceptable; fully air-gapped on-prem would be preferred only if the pricing delta is small.
3) Procurement: procurement@acme.com will need committed spend numbers and a suggested term (12 vs 24 months) with an outline of what is included in support and incident SLAs.

Can you include an example reserved commit breakdown that maps to the expected 18M tokens/day, and show the breakeven point versus hosted API for 12- and 24-month terms? Also please include an example of burst handling and how Redwood would handle overage.

We are cc'ing Emily from CloudOps — she will evaluate networking/VPC feasibility on our side and confirm any constraints.

Thanks — John

John — quick high-level numbers attached and a few assumptions so your procurement team can start review: 

Assumptions (please flag if any change):
- Workload: 18M tokens/day steady; 50M/day peak during events (assume 30-day month).
- Latency SLO: 99p <= 150ms (chat).
- Cache hit estimate: 12% (prefix/KV) — conservative.
- Model variant: Llama-3-like baseline; option to quantize to 4-bit for Dedicated/Private.

Summary (very coarse):
- Hosted API: per-token pricing gives lowest up-front but becomes costlier beyond ~12M tokens/day for 12-month term. Includes fully managed infra, automatic burst scaling, and TLS+SOC2 controls. No guaranteed dedicated throughput.
- Dedicated (Reserved): monthly committed GPU capacity priced below equivalent hosted per-token spend after breakeven. Commit tiers modelled at 2 GPU, 5 GPU, and 10 GPU pools. Suitable if you need predictable throughput and isolation without managing infra.
- Private VPC/On-prem: highest up-front implementation and networking costs; OPEX lower after operational stabilization. Required for strict data control and in-region residency.

Attachments: simplified scenario table with breakeven points and an example reserved commit breakdown mapped to your 18M tokens/day.

[Attachment: acme_tco_v1.xlsx (Excel, 45 KB)]

John / team — Vivek from Redwood SE here. A couple of technical notes that feed into the cost model and will affect the Dedicated vs Private decision: 

- Caching & Prefix reuse: If your product reuses prompts across many sessions (we saw examples on the call), effective token reduction of 8–15% is realistic. That improves hosted and dedicated economics.
- Batching & latency: For low-latency 99p targets we keep batch sizes small; that increases per-token cost compared to throughput-optimized batching. Dedicated pools can be tuned to achieve a better tradeoff if you accept slightly higher median latency.
- Quantization: Using 4-bit quantized model builds for Dedicated/Private can reduce GPU footprint by ~40% and materially lower commit needs.
- Networking: For VPC deployments we typically provide a control-plane tunnel and optional customer-managed KMS. Emily — if you share your VPC CIDRs and any proxy constraints we can validate the design.

I'll prepare a short runbook illustrating the latency vs cost tradeoffs and share it in the next email. Also happy to run a 45-minute deep-dive with your SREs to walk through the VPC implementation.
